summary: This PR archives the S-17 Bread calibration experiment, adding measurement harness and experiment-record tooling without touching production engine, API, or database behavior. The reviewer's findings are all minor or nit severity: two correctness edge cases (potential upscaling violating a documented contract in contact-sheet.py, and an unguarded baseline lookup that could throw instead of cleanly exiting in desktop-stats.ts), a missing-test gap for a risky custom resampler and exposure-stats logic that directly feeds the clipRatio metric central to this PR's purpose, and two cosmetic/documentation nits (dead code ternary, a stale path note). None of these affect production systems or introduce security risk, making this a reasonably clean, low-risk archival change with room for improvement in test coverage of its new measurement logic.

findings.description: `original.resize(target, Image.LANCZOS)` can upscale the original when it is smaller than the smallest output, breaking the docstring's matched-size contract ('An output is never enlarged; ... all are downscaled to the smallest') and the per-page 'every image at W×H' caption for the original figure.
findings.suggestion: Guard with a conditional resize and a visible note (like the differing-output-sizes note) when the original must be enlarged, or explicitly document that the original may be upscaled.

findings.description: point_bilinear — a hand-rolled canvas-emulating resampler whose rounding/support details directly move clipRatio across the 0.005 guard (per the module docstring) — has no automated tests, despite this PR existing because unreproducible numbers burned the team. Same for exposure_stats in scripts/measure-hue-shares.py (lines 124-129), whose denominators and thresholds are easy to silently regress.
findings.suggestion: Add small golden tests against fixed arrays (e.g. a known 4x4→2x2 point_bilinear case with the half-up rounding, an all-255 region asserting any=255 = 100%). They pin the method cheaply and match the repo's risk-weighted testing bar.

findings.description: compare() validates that the download contains each tuning id, but never checks the baseline side. With an old/partial baseline or a user-supplied --baseline file, `base[id]` is undefined and `auto(a)` / `a.clipRatio` throws a raw TypeError instead of the documented clean exit-1 'comparison could not run' path.
findings.suggestion: Add a mirrored `if (!a) { console.error(...); process.exit(1); }` check next to the existing `!b` check.

findings.description: `run.imageLabel.startsWith("data:") ? "(data URI)" : run.imageLabel` is dead code: imageLabel is `localPath ?? input.image`, so it is either a filesystem path or a remote URL, never a `data:` string. The guard implies a distinction that cannot occur.
findings.suggestion: Drop the ternary and record the label (or transport) directly.

findings.description: The run-record sidecar stores `output_file: dest` as an absolute OS-temp path. Once outputs are moved into the run directories contact-sheet.py scans (the documented workflow), that path is stale and misleading.
findings.suggestion: Drop the field or note in the header comment that it records the location at run time only; the sha256s are the durable identifiers.

implementation_correctness.justification: Two minor correctness gaps exist in auxiliary tooling: contact-sheet.py's resize can silently upscale the original image, violating its own documented matched-size contract (F1), and desktop-stats.ts compare() can throw an unhandled TypeError on a malformed/partial baseline instead of the documented clean exit path (F3). Both are edge-case failures in non-production scripts rather than core logic breaks, but they do contradict explicit documented behavior.

idiomaticity.justification: Only a minor stylistic nit was flagged: dead-code ternary logic in bread-spike.ts implies a distinction (data URI vs path) that can never occur (F4). No broader convention violations were reported.

complexity.justification: No findings indicate unnecessary complexity, over-engineering, or tangled logic; the reported issues are about missing edge-case handling and tests, not structural complexity.

test_risk_coverage.justification: The PR's stated motivation is avoiding unreproducible measurement numbers, yet the hand-rolled point_bilinear resampler and exposure_stats routines—whose rounding and thresholds directly affect reported clipRatio—have no automated tests (F2), despite the risk-weighted testing expectation this PR itself seems to validate against. This is a meaningful coverage gap for the specific risky logic the PR touches.

documentation.justification: Documentation is largely adequate per the findings, with only a minor nit that the run-record sidecar's stored output path becomes stale once files are relocated, without a note clarifying this (F5). No broader documentation gaps were raised.

security_safety.justification: No security, secret-handling, or untrusted-input findings were reported; this is an internal experiment-archival PR touching no production engine, API, or database behavior per the PR metadata.

verdictReason: All findings are minor or nit-level issues confined to auxiliary measurement/archival scripts rather than production code, with no security concerns and no criterion falling below 4; the missing tests for the resampling logic (F2) are the most notable gap but don't block the archival purpose of this PR.
